g.text: System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) — now called Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager (MECM) or Microsoft Configuration
Manager (ConfigMgr) — is Microsoft’s on-premises solution for managing large corporate IT environments.
SCCM is part of Microsoft Endpoint Manager, alongside Intune (cloud-native client management).
Primary Server → central SCCM site management, identified by a unique site code.
MSSQL Primary Database → stores client info, software, updates, and inventory.
SMS Provider → API layer between SCCM service and database, delivering
update/config data to clients and collecting status.
Distribution Point (DP) → distributes applications, OS images, and packages to clients.
Management Point (MP) → relays client configuration/status to SCCM servers.
Secondary Site Servers → optional, local database for bandwidth-limited locations.
Passive Site Servers → standby, activated if Primary Server fails.
Client Push Installation (default, least secure) → uses “client push accounts” (service accounts with local admin rights) to install
clients automatically. If one account fails, SCCM tries the next.
PXE boots machines over the network. While PXE doesn’t require SCCM, SCCM environments often have PXE boot support for OS
PXEThief is a Python tool (Windows-only, requires pywin32, works best with Python 3.10) for:
PXEThief interact with PXE boot media from SCCM DPs to
retrieve .boot.var and .boot.bcd files, possibly for cracking.
What it does: Sends DHCP PXE boot requests (broadcast or
targeted), downloads boot media, extracts hashes for cracking.
Crack PXE boot media password, decrypt media, extract stored AD credentials.

SCCM is optional — some organizations use it, others don’t.
The first audit step: check if SCCM is installed.
• SCCM modifies the Active Directory schema during deployment:
• Creates CN=System Management,CN=System container → contains site servers & roles.
SCCMHunter (Python) → Enumerates SCCM infrastructure and supports attack modules.
SharpSCCM (C#) → Enumeration, credential gathering, lateral movement from Windows.

Detects SCCM presence, site servers, roles, SMB signing status, PXEBoot
We use SCCMHunter or SharpSCCM to identify SCCM roles and extract sensitive files (PXEBoot variables) for later credential harvesting.
• Uses SMB enumeration to locate PXEBoot .var files.
• Identifies over-privileged accounts (sccm_push, sccm_naa, sccm_admin, sccm_sql) for privilege escalation.
$ python3 sccmhunter.py find -u blwasp -p Password123! -d lab.local -dc-ip 172.50.0.10
After reconnaissance, the objective is to gain higher privileges in the SCCM
1- Device Collection Variables → Key-value pairs used in deployments, may contain credentials.
2- Task Sequence Variables → Steps in OS/application deployment that can store credentials.
3- Network Access Accounts (NAA) → Domain accounts used to access content from the Distribution Point when machine accounts
cannot; sometimes configured with high privileges.
Stored credentials are usually DPAPI-encrypted → require local admin/privileged access to decrypt.
NAAs can also be obtained without compromising a host:
--> Impersonate a new machine to request SCCM policy and extract NAAs.
• Fake DDR reports → SCCM server attempts client installation on fake target.
• Triggers authentication from Client Push accounts (often local admins or higher).

• The Primary Server’s machine account must be in the local Administrators group on the DB
• If NTLM authentication from the Primary Server can be coerced and relayed to the DB
server’s SMB or MSSQL service, admin access can be gained.

Your user now has Full Administrator rights in SCCM, enabling complete control over the
• A WMI + REST API component that SCCM uses for management tasks.
• AdminService calls can directly manipulate SCCM objects (e.g., add administrators) without needing direct DB access.
• Local group granting access to both the WMI interface and AdminService API.
• If the Primary Site Server account is in this group on another server (SMS Provider server), and AdminService allows NTLM
auth, you can relay NTLM to add a Full Administrator.
• The HTTP(S) service for AdminService rarely enforces NTLM signing.
• Relay works without touching the DB directly — ntlmrelayx can complete the privilege escalation automatically.
• For HA setups, passive site servers often have local admin rights on the active site server and SCCM-wide admin rights.
• NTLM relay from passive → active server can yield a SOCKS session as an admin on the Primary Server.

SCCM purpose: Deploy applications, patches, and scripts on AD-managed assets. With admin rights on the Primary Site Server, an
attacker can move laterally, deploy payloads, or coerce authentication.
CMPivot: Admin service (HTTP REST API on Management Point via SMS Provider) → enumerate resources (software, admins,
Privileged accounts: Stored in SMS_Admin and SMS_SCI_Reserved WMI classes.
SharpSCCM: C# tool for enumeration & exploitation of SCCM.
sccmhunter.py: Python tool for SCCM interaction (admins, devices, collections, script execution, etc.).
Abuse: Deploy applications/scripts as SYSTEM, steal NTLM creds, perform NTLM relay, escalate privileges by adding admins.

MSSQL Server: Microsoft’s RDBMS (3rd most popular). Integrates tightly with AD & .NET.
Dialect: Uses T-SQL (procedural programming, local vars, extended functions).
impacket-mssqlclient: interact with MSSQL over SQL authentication, Windows auth, Kerberos, supports pass-the-hash.
SSMS (SQL Server Management Studio): GUI for managing MSSQL.
Execute T-SQL queries in query window.

Goal: Once sysadmin, next step is OS command execution.
xp_cmdshell → built-in extended stored procedure, spawns cmd.exe under sqlservr.exe. Disabled by default.
MSSQL Server Agent Jobs → abuse scheduled jobs. Can use subsystems: T-SQL, CmdExec, PowerShell. Requires SQLSERVERAGENT
OLE Automation Procedures → inter-process communication, can run commands (VBScript/COM objects). Disabled by default.
Config options: Use sp_configure + RECONFIGURE to enable advanced options, xp_cmdshell, or OLE automation.
Check if SQL Agent service is running (external observation or querying jobs).
Command Execution via MSSQL Server Agent Job
Add job step (PowerShell reverse shell payload):
Check configs → xp_cmdshell → SQL Agent Job → OLE Automation.
Always reset configs and delete jobs afterward for stealth
Linked Servers: MSSQL allows server-to-server queries. If Server A is linked to Server B, queries can be run on B from A.
OPENQUERY → run query on linked server (one result set).
EXECUTE AT → run query or stored procedure (multiple result sets, can run xp_cmdshell).
Use case for attackers: lateral movement to other SQL servers, remote command execution, credential theft.
SELECT * FROM OPENQUERY(SQL02, 'SELECT name, database_id, create_date

Connect with SSMS → ADMIN:SQL02 using sysadmin creds.

Exchange: Microsoft’s enterprise mail & calendar server. Current supported
EWS: SOAP over HTTP for apps.
Autodiscover: Connects with only username + password.
Global Address List (GAL): Catalog of AD user emails.
People view → roles, emails, phone numbers → useful for phishing.
Attack surface: public OWA, EWS, Autodiscover.
